name: url-router
title: URL Router
description: A router adapter for blocks that keep state in the URL: read the location, navigate, build an href and follow changes. hashRouter keeps a hash route's path (#/devices?device=a1), historyRouter the path and query string, memoryRouter is for tests; wrap your own router's API in the same shape.
docs: A `UrlRouter` is `{ read(): { path, params }, navigate(to, { replace }), href(to), subscribe(listener) }`. `hashRouter()` reads `#/path?query`, changes the query without touching the path and builds `#/path?query` hrefs, which fast links follow as hash routes; `historyRouter()` does the same with `location.pathname` and `location.search` and keeps the hash on writes. Both keep `history.state` and notify each other. `memoryRouter("/settings")` records `entries` for tests. `withParam(location, name, value)` sets or removes one param. Pass a router to `createUrlParam(name, { router })` (`master-detail`, `settings-page`) or `routerUrlState(router)` (`url-state`). When your router has a contract of its own (a path segment like `#/devices/<id>`), wrap its API in this shape, or skip the adapter and control the block (`selectedId` and `onSelectedIdChange`, `currentSection` and `onSectionChange`) from the route.
